lines: A rider might open Telo Ride on a small phone, or on a big screen across the room. Every screen has to fit both.
At three hundred and twenty pixels, the narrowest, every screen now fits: nothing scrolls sideways.
One didn't. The custom ride's clock, Pause and End ran five pixels past the edge. Now End wraps under the clock.
The page margin is sixteen pixels on a phone, twenty-four from small and thirty-two from large; content stops at eighty rem, centred.
At twenty-five sixty, the widest, Home sits in the middle, no wider than it reads well.
Fifteen screens are opened at both ends of the range on every run. The sweep through every breakpoint between waits until a person asks.
The custom ride, from a phone to the full screen.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
